Problem 9 Stereochemistry
Careful design of reactant structures and reaction conditions can provide highly selective stereochemical control.

9.1 Garner's aldehyde is frequently used for stereochemical control in synthesis. The route below prepares it from the natural product S-serine.

subquestions.text_open: 9.1.4 Garner's aldehyde can also be synthesized from R-serine. In the reaction below, replacing Boc with Ts reverses the selectivity. Explain why.

text_images.description: 'CC1(C)N([R])[C@@H](C=O)CO1'>Et-MgBr, THF>'CC1(C)N([R])[C@@H]([C@@H](O)CC)CO1' + 'CC1(C)N([R])[C@@H]([C@H](O)CC)CO1'. The image also states that the product ratio is 1:9 when R=Boc and 8:1 when R=Ts. R is the placeholder group used in the original diagram.

rubric: The oxygen atoms of the $SO_2$ sulfonyl group in Ts have low electron density and extremely weak coordinating ability, so a stable chelate cannot form (1 point). The direction of attack therefore more closely follows a nonchelation model, giving the other diastereomer with high selectivity (1 point). Calculations show a larger LUMO energy difference between the two reactive Felkin-Anh conformations of the N-Ts analogue; the orientation of the C-NTs bond thus produces a stronger reactive-conformation preference and enhances anti selectivity.
